For a Google Pixel 9 Pro XL, not seeing MCC/MNC is normal.

Use this:

- Name: Mint
- APN: wholesale
- MMSC: `http://wholesale.mmsmvno.com/mms/wapenc`
- MMS proxy: leave blank
- MMS port: leave blank
- APN type: `default,supl,mms`
- APN protocol: IPv4/IPv6

If MCC and MNC are missing, leave them alone. The SIM usually fills those in automatically.

On your Pixel, go here:
- Settings
- Network & internet
- SIMs
- Mint
- Access Point Names
- Tap `+` to add one, or edit the existing Mint APN
- Enter the values above
- Save
- Select that APN
- Restart the phone

If data or picture messages still do not work:
- turn Airplane Mode on, then off
- make sure Mobile data is on
- make sure roaming is on
- reset APNs to default, then add Mint again

Successfully able to transfer my cell number with my new Mint Mobile account. I bought two plans, so now I am wanting to access and set up another Mint Mobile plan on my son's phone. Does he need to do it from his phone? Do I just send him the email with the activation code, or what do I do?

An APN is the set of network instructions your phone uses to connect to your carrier’s mobile internet and picture messaging service.

Think of it like this:
- your phone knows how to talk to cell towers
- the **APN tells it where to go once it gets there**
- it tells the carrier how to route **cellular data**, **MMS/picture messages**, and sometimes hotspot features

Why you need to enter it:
When you switch carriers, your phone may still hold old network settings or fail to load the new ones correctly. Since Mint uses T-Mobile’s network and you came from Verizon, the phone sometimes needs the new routing info manually entered.

What an APN affects:
- mobile data / internet when not on Wi-Fi
- MMS, like picture messages and group texts
- sometimes hotspot/tethering
- sometimes visual voicemail, depending on carrier setup

What it does **not** affect:
- regular phone calls
- most basic SMS text messages
- your apps, photos, or files
- Wi-Fi connection

If APN settings are wrong, you might see:
- no internet unless on Wi-Fi
- picture messages not sending
- group texts failing or arriving weirdly
- hotspot not working
- slow or inconsistent cellular connection

Why there are so many fields:
Each one tells the carrier something specific:
- **APN**: the main network access point
- **MMSC**: where picture messages are sent
- **proxy/port**: extra routing instructions, if needed
- **APN type**: tells the phone what this APN should handle, like data and MMS
- **MCC/MNC**: network identification codes, often auto-filled by the SIM

On your Pixel, a lot of these are hidden because Android manages them automatically. That is why you do **not** need to panic if you cannot see every field.

What will be affected if you change them:
- If entered correctly, your data and MMS should work properly
- If entered incorrectly, mobile data or picture/group messaging may stop working until corrected
- It is usually reversible by tapping **Reset to default** in APN settings

So in plain English:
You are not changing anything dangerous. You are just telling your Pixel how to use Mint’s network for internet and multimedia messages.

For your Pixel 9 Pro XL with Mint, the most important parts are usually:
- APN: `wholesale`
- MMSC: `http://wholesale.mmsmvno.com/mms/wapenc`
- APN type: `default,supl,mms`

Everything else is often blank or auto-handled.

He does **not** have to do it from his phone, but it is usually easiest to **activate the second Mint plan while physically holding his phone** because you may need to:

- insert the Mint SIM or enable the eSIM on **his** device
- enter the activation code
- confirm the phone’s IMEI if asked
- set up APN/data settings on **his** phone afterward

What you usually do:
1. Open the Mint app or Mint Mobile activation page
2. Sign into the account you used to buy the plans
3. Choose the second line/plan
4. Use the **activation code** for that specific plan
5. Complete setup on **your son’s phone**

So yes, you can **send him the email with the activation code**, but he will still likely need to do a few steps on his own phone unless you are with him and can do it for him.

A few important things:
- If he wants to **keep his current number**, do **not** activate until you have his transfer info ready:
  - account number
  - transfer PIN
  - billing ZIP code from his old carrier
- If he is getting a **new number**, activation is easier
- If the plan is **eSIM**, it usually needs to be installed directly on his phone
- If it is a **physical SIM**, you can give him the SIM card and activation code, then complete setup on his device

Best practical answer:
- **If you’re together:** do it on his phone
- **If you’re apart:** forward him the activation email/code and walk him through it, but the final setup should happen on his phone

make sure you know whether his second Mint line is **physical SIM or eSIM**, and whether he is **transferring a number or getting a new one**.

That makes sense. Once your Verizon number transfer completed, Verizon may have changed the login, ownership, or account access, so you may no longer have what you need to port your son’s line.

As customer support, I’d tell you this:

Your son’s number can usually **still be moved**, but you need the **Verizon transfer details for his line**, specifically:
- Verizon account number
- Verizon Number Transfer PIN
- Billing ZIP code
- Confirmation that the line is still active

Important part:
**Do not cancel his Verizon line first.** It has to stay active until Mint finishes porting it.

What likely happened:
- your line was transferred successfully
- Verizon account access changed or got locked down
- now you cannot retrieve the transfer PIN or manage the remaining line

What to do next:
1. Call Verizon customer service or Number Transfer support
2. Explain that **one line was already ported out**, but you still need to **port your son’s active line**
3. Ask them for:
   - the account number
   - a fresh Number Transfer PIN for your son’s line
   - confirmation of the billing ZIP code on file
4. Then use that info to activate your son’s Mint line

What to say to Verizon:
:::writing{variant="chat_message" id="48216"}
Hi, I already transferred my own number out, but I still need to port my son’s active Verizon line to Mint Mobile. I no longer have access to the Verizon account details I need. Can you please help me get the account number, the Number Transfer PIN for his line, and confirm the billing ZIP code so I can complete the transfer? His line is still active and I do not want it canceled.
:::

If Verizon says you are not authorized:
- the **account owner** may need to call
- or your son may need to be made an account manager if he is eligible
- or Verizon may require identity verification before releasing the transfer info

If your son is on a separate line but under the same family account, Verizon will often still treat it as controlled by the main account owner.

One more thing:
If you already bought the Mint plan, that is fine. You do **not** need to use the activation code yet until you have the Verizon port-out info.

If you want, I can help you draft exactly what to say to Verizon if they push back.

On a Pixel 9 Pro XL, those fields are often hidden or auto-managed, so the fix is usually to edit only the fields Google lets you touch.

No. Do **not** put `8080` in the regular **Port** field.

On your Pixel:
- **Port** = for the main APN internet proxy port
- **MMS port** = separate field just for picture/group messages

If your Pixel only shows **Port** and does **not** show a separate **MMS port** field, then:

- leave **Port** blank
- leave **MMS proxy** blank
- do **not** enter `8080` there

For Mint on a Pixel, use:
- **APN:** `wholesale`
- **MMSC:** `http://wholesale.mmsmvno.com/mms/wapenc`
- **Port:** blank
- **Proxy:** blank
- **MMS proxy:** blank
- **APN type:** `default,supl,mms`

Then save it, select it, and restart the phone.

The main thing is this: **8080 only belongs in MMS port**, and if your phone does not give you an MMS port field, you usually just leave it out.

Got it, this is a super common issue when switching carriers (especially going from entity["company","Verizon","US telecom carrier"] to entity["company","Mint Mobile","US prepaid carrier"]).

Here’s what’s actually going on and how to fix it 👇

---

## Why you can’t find MCC / MNC
- **MCC (Mobile Country Code)** and **MNC (Mobile Network Code)** are usually **auto-filled by the SIM**
- Many phones **hide or lock these fields**
- On some devices, they **don’t appear at all** unless you manually create a new APN

👉 So you’re not doing anything wrong. Your phone just isn’t showing them.

---

## Mint Mobile APN Settings (Correct Values)
If you’re setting this up manually, use:

- **Name:** Mint  
- **APN:** wholesale  
- **MMSC:** http://wholesale.mmsmvno.com/mms/wapenc  
- **MMS Proxy:** (leave blank)  
- **MMS Port:** (leave blank)  
- **MCC:** 310  
- **MNC:** 260  
- **APN Type:** default,supl,mms  
- **APN Protocol:** IPv4/IPv6  

---

## What to do if MCC / MNC are missing

### Option 1: Leave them alone (recommended)
If your phone:
- auto-fills them
- or doesn’t show them

👉 **Do NOT try to force it**  
Just enter everything else and save.

---

### Option 2: Reset APN settings
Sometimes old entity["company","Verizon","US telecom carrier"] settings interfere.

**Steps:**
- Go to Settings → Cellular/Mobile Network  
- Access Point Names  
- Tap the 3 dots → **Reset to default**

Then re-enter Mint settings.

---

### Option 3: Add a new APN manually
If nothing works:
- Tap **Add / +**
- Enter the Mint settings above
- Save it
- Select it as active

---

## Important troubleshooting checks
If MMS or data still isn’t working:

- Toggle **Airplane Mode ON → OFF**
- Restart your phone
- Make sure **Mobile Data is ON**
- Make sure **Data Roaming is ON** (Mint sometimes requires this)
- Confirm your SIM is fully activated

---

## One key thing people miss
Mint runs on entity["company","T-Mobile","US telecom carrier"]’s network.

👉 So your phone is basically trying to switch from Verizon’s network profile to T-Mobile’s  
Sometimes it takes a reset + reboot for everything to “lock in.”

---

Tell me:
- iPhone or Android  
- Exact model  

And I’ll give you **step-by-step taps for your exact screen** so you don’t have to guess.
